steps.title: Import Vue and ref from vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the vue package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a package
import { ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Vue APIs for reactive state management are imported.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've imported Vue and ref, which are essential for creating reactive state in Vue components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the useFeatureFlag hook function
steps.instruction: Create a function called useFeatureFlag that returns an empty object.
steps.hint: Define a function with the name useFeatureFlag and have it return {}.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and ref from 'vue'

// Create the useFeatureFlag hook function
steps.expectedOutcome: A useFeatureFlag function is defined and returns an empty object.
successCriteria: The useFeatureFlag function exists and returns an object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the custom hook function. Next we'll add state to it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function is named exactly useFeatureFlag and returns an object (even if empty).
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named useFeatureFlag that returns {}.

steps.title: Add feature flag state using ref
steps.instruction: Inside the useFeatureFlag hook function, create a reactive state variable called isEnabled using ref, initialized to false.
steps.hint: Use the ref function you imported earlier to create reactive state. The syntax is: const isEnabled = ref(false);
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating reactive state with ref
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFeatureFlag hook will have a reactive isEnabled state variable initialized to false.
successCriteria: The useFeatureFlag hook contains a const isEnabled = ref(false); declaration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the reactive feature flag state using ref.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using ref() to create the reactive state and initializing it to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The isEnabled reactive state wasn't created correctly. Remember to use ref(false) inside the hook function.

steps.title: Add toggle function to the hook
steps.instruction: Inside the useFeatureFlag function, define a function named toggle that toggles the isEnabled value.
steps.hint: You can create a function that updates the isEnabled ref value to its opposite boolean state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFeatureFlag function now contains a toggle function that will switch the isEnabled state between true and false.
successCriteria: A toggle function is defined inside useFeatureFlag that toggles the isEnabled value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the toggle function to your feature flag hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your toggle function properly toggles the isEnabled value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle function is missing or doesn't toggle the isEnabled value correctly.

steps.title: Return state and toggle from the hook
steps.instruction: Inside the useFeatureFlag function, return an object containing the isEnabled state and toggle function.
steps.hint: Make sure to return an object with both properties so components can use them.
steps.expectedOutcome: The hook now exposes its state and toggle function for components to use.
successCriteria: The useFeatureFlag function returns an object containing isEnabled and toggle.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned the reactive state and toggle function from your custom hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning an object with both isEnabled and toggle properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook should return an object containing both the isEnabled state and toggle function.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'FeatureFlagDemo' with a setup function that returns an empty template.
steps.hint: Define a component function that returns an object from its setup function. The template can be empty for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A component named 'FeatureFlagDemo' is defined with a setup function that returns an empty object.
successCriteria: The component 'FeatureFlagDemo' is defined as a function with a setup function that returns an object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main Vue component. Next, we'll implement the feature flag hook inside it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you define a function named 'FeatureFlagDemo' with a setup function that returns an object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named 'FeatureFlagDemo' with a setup function that returns an object.

steps.title: Use the feature flag hook in the component
steps.instruction: Inside your component's setup function, call the useFeatureFlag hook and destructure the returned isEnabled and toggle values.
steps.hint: Call the hook and destructure the object it returns: const { isEnabled, toggle } = useFeatureFlag();
steps.expectedOutcome: The component's setup function now has access to the feature flag state and toggle function from the custom hook.
successCriteria: The useFeatureFlag hook is called inside the component setup, and isEnabled and toggle are destructured from its return value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used the custom hook in your component. The isEnabled and toggle values are now available for use in your template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useFeatureFlag() and destructuring both isEnabled and toggle from the returned object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook isn't being used correctly. You need to call useFeatureFlag() inside the component setup and destructure the returned values.

steps.title: Return the reactive state and toggle from setup
steps.instruction: In your component's setup function, return an object containing isEnabled and toggle to make them available in the template.
steps.hint: The setup function should return an object with the properties you want to expose to the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The setup function returns an object with isEnabled and toggle, making them accessible in the template.
successCriteria: The setup function returns an object containing both isEnabled and toggle.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've returned the reactive state and toggle function from setup, making them available for use in the template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning an object with both isEnabled and toggle properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The setup function needs to return an object containing both isEnabled and toggle.

steps.title: Add template structure with feature flag status
steps.instruction: In your Vue component's template section, add a paragraph element that displays the current feature flag status using the isEnabled reactive value.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to display reactive values in the template. The paragraph should show something like 'Feature flag is: enabled' or 'Feature flag is: disabled' based on the isEnabled value.
steps.analogousExample: // Displaying reactive state in template
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain a paragraph that dynamically displays whether the feature flag is enabled or disabled based on the reactive isEnabled value.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the template that displays the isEnabled value using Vue's template interpolation syntax {{ }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a paragraph that displays the current feature flag status. The template now shows the dynamic state of your feature flag.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct syntax to display the isEnabled value in the template. Remember to use double curly braces {{ }} around the reactive value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet show the feature flag status. Add a paragraph element that displays the isEnabled value using Vue's template interpolation syntax.

steps.title: Add toggle button and wire click event
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside your template that calls the toggle function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to bind the toggle function to the button's click event.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include a button that toggles the feature flag state when clicked.
successCriteria: A button element with @click="toggle" is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an interactive button that toggles the feature flag.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it's wired to the toggle function using @click.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly connected to the toggle function.
